tierWhy: instrument scoping measurement; no money path, no product diff
headline: THE SCOPING ERROR IS REAL BUT IT IS NOT THE API — IT IS THE SURFACE. My harness has been measuring a 2-document, 75 MB chart shell while the PO drives an 11-18 document, 383 MB page. Same metric, different page. Meanwhile the API claim fails again on measurement: performance.memory reads 1.22x HIGHER than the figure Performance Monitor shows, and Chrome's precision flag changes nothing (75.36 vs 75.37 MB).

whatIOwn.concession: the Director's instinct that every memory figure in this plan is scoped wrong is CORRECT, and I am the reason. My floor is 61-75 MB against his 383 MB on the same metric — a 5-6x surface gap. I have been grading cuts on a lighter page than the product the PO uses, and that plausibly contributed to the 12-vs-25 MB/cycle disagreement all week.
whatIOwn.correctionToTheMechanism: the gap is NOT that usedJSHeapSize reads the main frame only. Three independent measurements say otherwise (below). It is that my harness loads /chart/dist-v9/index.html?mode=backtest&mcLayout=1 — a bare chart shell with ONE document — and the PO loads the full application.
whatIOwn.consequence: re-baselining on the PO's actual route is the priority, and it needs the route named. Until then my absolute floors are not comparable to his; my A/B deltas remain internally valid because both arms ran on the same surface.

precisionHypothesis.idea: every harness here passes --enable-precise-memory-info and the PO's Chrome does not; Chrome quantizes performance.memory without it, which could make his console readings coarse
precisionHypothesis.test: same build, same route, flag ON vs OFF, two runs each, reading performance.memory and CDP Performance.getMetrics at the same instant
precisionHypothesis.result: FALSIFIED. perf.memory 75.36 / 76.06 MB with the flag and 75.37 / 75.44 MB without it. The flag is not the explanation.
precisionHypothesis.keptAnyway: the switch is now in the harness behind TALARIA_HEAP_NO_PRECISE_MEMORY with unit tests, because it is the only way to reproduce the PO's browser configuration on demand

ratioToPerformanceMonitorMetric.readingWithW86: W86 gave 18 same-instant samples at 0.695 (cdpUsed/perfMemory); these four agree at 1.22 the other way up. Across 22 samples performance.memory has NEVER read a fraction of the Performance Monitor figure — it reads consistently higher.
ratioToPerformanceMonitorMetric.soTheReferenceInstruction: I will report BOTH gauges from now on rather than swapping to one, because on my surface they disagree by a knowable 1.22x and neither is a fraction of the other. If the Director still wants Performance Monitor's number as the single reference, JSHeapUsedSize from Performance.getMetrics IS that number and it is already recorded at every sample.

floorCensus.question: name what those documents ARE and what the 383 MB consists of
floorCensus.firstRealFinding: the Documents counter reads 2 while the frame tree contains exactly ONE frame. The counter therefore includes documents that are not frames — an initial about:blank or a detached document. CONSEQUENCE: '11-18 documents' is NOT '11-18 iframes', and neither is my own W86 staircase. Any argument that counts documents as panels is wrong by construction.
floorCensus.whatICannotName: his 383 MB and 11-18 documents are not on my surface, so I cannot itemise them from here. Candidates, in the order I would test them: the application wrapper and route he loads (my shell has no app chrome at all), a saved layout restoring tiles at load, browser extensions in his profile injecting frames, and DevTools itself.
threeSixtySecondTestsForThePo: In the console on the FRESH chart: Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('iframe')).map(f => f.src || '(no src)') — itemises every frame the page owns, by URL.
Reload the same page in an INCOGNITO window with extensions disabled and re-read documents and JS heap size. If 11-18 becomes 2-3, the floor is his profile, not our product.
Chrome Task Manager (Shift+Esc): how many renderer rows for the app tab, and each row's JavaScript memory. Still the cleanest explanation for a whole-tab figure exceeding a per-isolate one.
floorCensus.blockerForMe: the exact URL/route the PO loads for a 'fresh single chart'. One line from him or B and I re-baseline everything on it.

baselineNondeterminism.question: 13 documents on one fresh load, 18 on another, same pairs, same hard refresh — name it
baselineNondeterminism.onMySurface: DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Four fresh loads: documents 2/2/2/2, frames 2/2/2/2, nodes 6324/6225/6228/6226, listeners 1348/1349/1348/1348, heap 75.36/75.37/76.06/75.44 MB. Spread under 1%.
baselineNondeterminism.whatThatNarrowsTo: the varying component is not in the chart shell. It is in the surrounding application, the restored layout, or his browser profile — the same three candidates as the floor, which is suggestive: whatever adds 9-16 documents is also what makes the count vary.
baselineNondeterminism.honestLimit: a deterministic bare shell does not prove the app wrapper is the varying part. It proves the chart shell is not.

onTheRetractedStaircase.agreed: my own W86 counter data has the same lag artefact in it. I read documents at the collapsed floor after a forced collection, which is the right moment, but I did not measure the settle time the PO observed, and I did not run between-session repeats to see whether the drift exceeds session-to-session variance. My +8 documents over four cycles was one run per arm — the exact error W84 taught me and I repeated it eight hours later.
onTheRetractedStaircase.whatSurvivesFromW86: the DOM-COUNTER-STAIRCASE-V1 cell itself is still worth having, but its threshold is now wrong: a tolerance of one document cannot stand when between-session variance is larger than the drift. It needs a settle wait and a repeat-based threshold before it grades anything.
onTheRetractedStaircase.actionTaken: I am not leaving a gate cell in place that would produce a confident RED on noise. Next packet: settle wait, N-session baseline spread, threshold derived from that spread — or the cell comes out.

declaration: Nothing declared. Per DECL-01 the per-cycle question is open until the PO's Performance Monitor sequence lands, and my instrument agrees it is open.
